subject: business-studies
title: Globalisation Drivers and MNCs
welcome_lead: Why has the world shrunk - and what do multinationals do with that?
meta_desc: A-Level Global Business: globalisation drivers and the role of MNCs.
final_note: Globalisation lifts opportunity and risk in equal measure.

walkthroughs.body_html: Falling transport costs (containerisation), digital communication, trade liberalisation via the WTO and the rise of emerging markets all combined to shrink distance.
MNCs allocate production across borders to exploit cost differences, skills and tax regimes. They can transfer technology and create jobs - but also dominate local markets and avoid tax.
Long supply chains are vulnerable to pandemics, geopolitics and climate shocks. Many firms are now reshoring or nearshoring to cut these risks.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
The level of output where total revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss. It is NOT the level where profit is maximised; profit grows beyond break-even.
Break-even is where the business makes the most profit.
Economies of scale means a business saves the economy money.
